title: Finite-height descent of the input valuation algebra
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], $V\subseteq K$ a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, and $A$ a flat finitely presented commutative $V$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] such that $A_K=A\otimes_VK$ is geometrically reduced. Then there exist a separably closed subfield $K_0\subseteq K$, its valuation subring $V_0=V\cap K_0$ of finite height, and a flat finitely presented $V_0$-algebra $A_0$ with geometrically reduced $A_0\otimes_{V_0}K_0$, together with a $V$-algebra isomorphism $A_0\otimes_{V_0}V\cong A$. The inclusion $V_0\to V$ is local and faithfully flat. The fields $K_0$ and $K$ need not be equal and the tensor product uses the inclusion $V_0\to V$. Zero algebras and height zero valuations are included.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, first sentence of Step 5, printed p. 24, using Corollary 2.1.3(ii), printed p. 8 (Step 5 misprints this reference as Lemma 2.1.1(ii)); finite-presentation descent made explicit; primary PDF read online, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], choose a presentation $A\cong V[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. Let $C\subset V$ be the finite set of coefficients of these finitely many polynomials. Let $F\subseteq K$ be the subfield generated by the prime subfield and $C$. It is finitely generated as a field over its prime subfield, including when $C$ is empty. For each nonzero $x\in F$, either $x$ or $x^{-1}$ lies in $V\cap F$, because the same alternative holds in $V$ and both elements belong to $F$. Thus $W=V\cap F$ is a valuation ring of $F$, and every element of $F$ is a fraction of elements of $W$.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 5, printed p. 24; finite presentation makes Corollary 2.1.3(ii) applicable through the finite coefficient set. Expanded argument by Q65.

proof.text: Let $K_0\subseteq K$ be the separable algebraic closure of $F$ in $K$ from [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]; $K$ is separably closed in that node's root sense, as an irreducible separable $g$ of degree $\ge2$ would give the nontrivial finite separable extension $K[T]/(g)$. So $K_0/F$ is algebraic and $K_0$ is separably closed, hence by [lem-pc-sepclosed-finite-sep-trivial] also in the sense of [def-kun-separably-closed]. Put $V_0=V\cap K_0$, a valuation ring with fraction field $K_0$ by restricting the valuation alternative. By [lem-trf-abhyankar-finite-type-field-height], $W$ has height at most $\operatorname{trdeg}(F)+1$. By [lem-trf-valuation-algebraic-height] for $K_0/F$ and $V_0$, with $V_0\cap F=W$, $V_0$ has the same finite height. Every coefficient in $C$ lies in $V_0$.

source.place: Section 2.1, Corollary 2.1.3(i)-(ii), printed p. 8, and the algebraic value-group/height discussion on printed p. 7; separable closure inside K as in Stacks fields.tex, Tags 09HC and 09HB.

proof.text: The inclusion $V_0\subseteq V$ is local. Here is the elementary local-ring check for either valuation ring $R$. Its nonunits form a proper ideal: multiplication by an element of $R$ cannot turn a nonunit into a unit; if nonzero $r,s$ are nonunits, the valuation alternative gives $r/s\in R$ or $s/r\in R$, and $r+s=s(1+r/s)$ or $r(1+s/r)$ is a nonunit. Zero summands and negatives cause no difficulty. Every proper ideal contains only nonunits, so this ideal is the unique maximal ideal. For $u\in V_0\setminus\{0\}$, its inverse belongs to $K_0$, and therefore $u^{-1}\in V$ if and only if $u^{-1}\in V\cap K_0=V_0$. Thus an element of $V_0$ is a unit in $V$ exactly when it is a unit in $V_0$. The maximal ideal of $V$ contracts to that of $V_0$, including when either valuation is trivial.

source.place: Valuation-ring fraction-field characterization, Tag 00IB; elementary proof of locality and the contraction of nonunits is written out here.

proof.text: The $V_0$-module $V$ is torsion-free: if $a\in V_0$ is nonzero and $av=0$ in $V$, the same equality in the field $K$ gives $v=0$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] with valuation ring $V_0$ and module $V$ to obtain flatness. Step 3 supplies local rings and a local inclusion, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] makes $V_0\to V$ faithfully flat.

Regard each $f_j$ as a polynomial $f_{j,0}\in V_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with the same coefficients and set $A_0=V_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_{1,0},\ldots,f_{m,0})$. This is a finitely presented $V_0$-algebra by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] to this quotient and $V_0\to V$. It gives $A_0\otimes_{V_0}V\cong V[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\cong A$ as $V$-algebras, with each polynomial variable mapping to the original chosen generator. Thus the tensor product and its scalar structure use the actual inclusion $V_0\to V$.

source.place: Tag 00F3, definition-finite-type, part (2), and Section 05G3, section-base-change, polynomial presentation formula immediately after Definition 05G4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flatness-descends-faithfully-flat] with $R=V_0$, $R\prime=V$ and $M=A_0$. Its tensor module $V\otimes_{V_0}A_0$ identifies with $A$ using Step 5 and the flip $v\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes v$, whose inverse is the same flip. Both preserve the $V$-action, so this module is flat over $V$ by hypothesis. Step 4 gives the required faithfully flat base map. The cited equivalence therefore proves that $A_0$ is flat over $V_0$.

source.place: Tag 00HJ, lemma-flatness-descends, applied to the algebra as its underlying module.

proof.text: Put $B_0=A_0\otimes_{V_0}K_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change], $B_0$ has the finite presentation $K_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_{1,0},\ldots,f_{m,0})$, so it is finitely presented over $K_0$. Apply the same node to this presentation along $K_0\subseteq K$: $B_0\otimes_{K_0}K$ is $K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. Applying the node to the original presentation of $A$ along $V\subseteq K$ gives this very same presentation for $A_K=A\otimes_VK$. The identity on $K$ and on all variables therefore gives a $K$-algebra isomorphism $B_0\otimes_{K_0}K\cong A_K$. Its inverse is the identity on the same generators. In particular the left side is geometrically reduced over $K$ by hypothesis.

source.place: Section 05G3, section-base-change, formula for coefficient base change of a polynomial quotient; applied to V_0 to K_0, K_0 to K, and V to K.

proof.text: Apply the base-change equality in [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-fibre-locus] to the finitely presented map $K_0\to B_0$ and the field inclusion $a:K_0\to K$. Step 7 verifies finite presentation and says that $B_0\otimes_{K_0}K$ is geometrically reduced. The spectra of $K_0$ and $K$ each have exactly the single prime $(0)$, with residue fields $K_0$ and $K$. The equality $E_{\mathrm{red}}((B_0\otimes_{K_0}K)/K)=(\operatorname{Spec}a)^{-1}(E_{\mathrm{red}}(B_0/K_0))$ therefore forces $(0)\in E_{\mathrm{red}}(B_0/K_0)$. This says precisely that $B_0=A_0\otimes_{V_0}K_0$ is geometrically reduced over $K_0$. Together with Steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 this proves all the assertions. The argument uses neither a nonzero algebra nor a positive valuation height.

source.place: Tag 0576, lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced; only the base-change equality of the cited node is used, not its constructibility assertion.

split_report.summary: Expanded Temkin’s finite-height reduction into eight steps. Choose a finitely generated coefficient subfield, take its relative separable closure inside K, preserve finite height by algebraic height invariance, prove the valuation inclusion local and faithfully flat, descend the polynomial presentation and flatness, and detect geometric reducedness with the existing fibre-locus base-change equality. Reuses existing nodes only; no new nodes, no attachment, and no mathematical change to the statement.
